factor_scores.evidence_summary: 13 distinct audit engagements across 7 firms covering core USDe contracts. V2 contracts (EthenaMinting V2, StakedUSDeV2) audited by Pashov (May 23 2024) prior to V2 deploy (July 8 2024). Etherscan verified source on all four core contracts. All audits completed pre-deploy per official docs. No critical or high findings across any engagement. Commit SHA not publicly disclosed, so bytecode-to-commit match is medium confidence, but no evidence of scope mismatch.

Most recent audit covering core USDe contracts is Pashov V2 (May 23 2024), covering EthenaMinting V2 and StakedUSDeV2. As of 2026-04-28 this is approximately 706 days (~23 months). ENA audited by Pashov Sep 2 2024 (~600 days). No audit has been published for any post-July 2024 changes. Core architecture is unchanged since V2 deploy, reducing drift risk, but 23-month recency gap is notable.

Code4rena 2023 found 4 mediums: M-01 (confirmed fixed), M-02 (disputed — team maintains it is not an invariant), M-03 (confirmed fixed), M-04 (acknowledged, mitigated by deployment practice only). Code4rena 2024 found 2 mediums: M-01 (fixed via PR #2), M-02 (acknowledged/disputed severity). No case where finding is marked Resolved without on-chain change evidence. Two Acknowledged-Disputed mediums create residual ambiguity: M-04 2023 DoS via MinShares is unpatched at contract level.

13 distinct engagements across 7 firms: Zellic (1), Quantstamp (2), Spearbit/Cantina (1), Pashov (5), Code4rena (2 contests), Chaos Labs (economic, 1+), Cyfrin (1). Discounting Chaos Labs as economic-only, 12 code security engagements. Exceptional audit density for a 26-month-old protocol.

Tier-1 firms: Spearbit/Cantina, Zellic. Tier-2: Quantstamp, Cyfrin, Code4rena competitive contests. Boutique: Pashov Audit Group (4 engagements). Economic specialist: Chaos Labs. Strong firm diversity for the protocol's size and age.

V1 contracts: multiple audits Oct-Nov 2023, mainnet launch Feb 19 2024 — approximately 90-120 days post-audit. V2: Pashov audit May 23 2024, V2 deployed July 8 2024 — 46 days. Both within acceptable range. 46 days for V2 is slightly tight but not a red flag given prior extensive V1 coverage.

Active Immunefi bug bounty program live since April 4 2024. Max payout $3M for critical smart contract vulnerabilities (10% of affected funds, min $100K). 27 assets in scope. Core contracts (USDe, EthenaMinting V2, StakedUSDeV2, ENA, USDeSilo, EthenaLPStaking, StakingRewardsDistributor) confirmed in scope.

No post-mortem evidence of a disclosed vulnerability that was reported to the team and ignored before exploit. No smart contract exploits of Ethena core contracts have occurred as of 2026-04-28. April 2026 LayerZero bridge suspension was precautionary (not an exploit of Ethena's own contracts).

No formal verification (Certora, Halmos, Kani) has been published for Ethena contracts. Chaos Labs provided economic risk analysis only (not FV). No FV coverage found in any of the 13 audit engagements.

No public Slither/Mythril/Semgrep run output published for Ethena deployed bytecode. Code4rena 2023 (competitive audit included automated tool use) found 0 high-severity findings and 4 mediums. Code4rena 2024 invitational found 0 high-severity findings and 2 mediums. True-positive high-severity count from systematic static analysis is not independently verifiable. Marked yellow as a programmatic gap, not because findings were identified.
Source inspection of USDe, EthenaMinting, StakedUSDeV2, StakedUSDe, USDeSilo shows no selfdestruct opcode in any contract. All contracts are non-upgradeable direct implementations.

No delegatecall usage found in USDe, EthenaMinting V2, StakedUSDeV2, or USDeSilo. All contracts are direct implementations with no proxy or delegatecall pattern. Confirmed via source inspection and Etherscan ABI review.

No arbitrary call pattern found in inspected contracts. EthenaMinting uses ECDSA.recover() for authenticated minting/redemption. External calls are limited to allowlisted custodian addresses and the USDe token contract. No user-supplied target address for arbitrary external calls.

StakedUSDe implements OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard on transferInRewards(), _deposit(), _withdraw(). EthenaMinting V2 implements nonReentrant on mint(), redeem(), transferToCustody(). USDe has no external calls in critical paths requiring reentrancy guard.

Protocol does not integrate ERC-777 or ERC-1155 token standards. Collateral for minting is limited to allowlisted assets (stablecoins, LSTs — all standard ERC-20s). USDe itself is ERC-20 without hooks. No ERC-777 callback integration surface identified.

No divide-before-multiply finding documented in any of the 13 audit engagements or Code4rena reports. Code4rena 2023 (588 nSLOC, 98 low/NC findings) did not flag this at any severity. Absence of finding is positive but not fully programmatically confirmed.

EthenaMinting V2 uses allowlisted collateral assets. Price validation applies Chainlink oracle feeds (standard 8-decimal). Pashov V2 audit and Code4rena found no mixed-decimals vulnerability. No confirmed instance of this pattern.

Solidity 0.8.19/0.8.20 with default overflow protection (SafeMath built-in). No signed/unsigned confusion vulnerability documented in any audit. Pashov Oct 2024 (USDtb scope) found L-03 EIP712 type mismatch uint128/uint120 in UStbMinting, but this is the USDtb sub-product and is out of core USDe scope.

EthenaMinting V2 uses OpenZeppelin ECDSA.recover() which internally validates that the returned address is not address(0). No raw ecrecover without zero-address guard found. OZ ECDSA library is the gold standard for this check.

EthenaMinting V2 implements EIP-712 with chainId validation: caches _chainId and recomputes domain separator on chain ID change. Cross-chain replay is prevented. EIP-712 domain separator includes chainId by construction.

None of the core Ethena contracts use UUPS or any proxy pattern. USDe, EthenaMinting V2, StakedUSDeV2 are all direct non-upgradeable implementations. UUPS _authorizeUpgrade gate factor is not applicable. USDtb (sub-product) uses upgradeable pattern but is out of core scope.

All four core contracts use constructor-based initialization. USDe: constructor(address admin). EthenaMinting V2: constructor(IUSDe _usde, IWETH9 _weth, address[] _assets, ...). StakedUSDeV2: constructor(IERC20 _asset, address initialRewarder, address owner). ENA: constructor-based. No initialize() function on any implementation contract. One-tx exploit vector does not exist.

Not applicable — none of the core contracts use a proxy pattern. _disableInitializers() is only relevant for proxy-behind-implementation patterns (EIP-1967, UUPS, transparent proxy). No proxy architecture exists in core Ethena contracts.

V1 contest scope: 6 contracts, 588 nSLOC. V2 invitational scope: 4 contracts, 665 nSLOC. Multiple overlapping audits cover the same contracts. High audit density per line of code. Multiple independent reviews (competitive + boutique) further reduce missed-complexity risk.

Ethena documents a protocol multisig and a separate Dev Multisig; the public contract and documentation reviewed do not establish an on-chain timelock for the relevant admin path. The documented multisig architecture leaves meaningful key-management risk.

Dev Multisig 5-of-11 confirmed via Safe API. Reserve Fund 4-of-10 confirmed. sUSDe Payout Fund 3-of-11 claimed but Safe API not_found. DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE multisig '7/10 or more' per docs but address not published on-chain.
No single EOA admin. USDe owner = Dev Multisig 5-of-11 (0x3B0AAf...). EthenaMinting limits managed by Dev Multisig per docs. Deployer (0x8de54b1...) transferred admin to multisig before/at launch.

Ethena documents a protocol multisig with a high nominal signature threshold, while the public Dev Multisig record identifies a separate 5-of-11 operational Safe. The separate public descriptions do not establish a single, independently attributable signer posture for all privileged paths; yellow remains.
factor_scores.notes: Factual correction #21; decision posted 2026-06-24; second-review applied where required.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Docs claim geographic distribution and custody diversity (internal + external stakeholders including market makers and exchanges). Cannot independently verify ASN/custodian co-hosting at OSINT tier. Green claim in docs is plausible but unverified.
Docs state all multisig keys are cold wallets. Cannot independently verify signing device types via on-chain heuristics at OSINT tier. Documented claim accepted at low confidence.
No public, date-bounded signer-set change history sufficient to assess threshold drift was located.
factor_scores.notes: Public documentation identifies the current governance roles but does not provide a complete, date-bounded signer-change history for this factor.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: The public documentation describes multisig governance and a time-lock process, but the reviewed minting contract source shows privileged configuration is controlled through admin roles rather than a public TimelockController address. The on-chain-enforceable delay for the critical admin path is not substantiated; red remains.

No timelock verified on any sensitive function: mint limit changes, collateral add/remove, rescueTokens, redistributeLockedAmounts, role grants all execute immediately after multisig consensus. GATEKEEPER_ROLE can disable mint/redeem without timelock. DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can change role assignments without timelock.

GATEKEEPER_ROLE exists in EthenaMinting, held by Ethena Labs staff and external third parties (market makers, exchanges). Gatekeepers can only disable mint/redeem (cannot re-enable — re-enable requires DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE). Meaningful separation of pause-keeper from upgrade/admin role.

No upgrade function exists (non-upgradeable contracts). Roles are separated at contract level: MINTER_ROLE, REDEEMER_ROLE, GATEKEEPER_ROLE distinct from DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE. However, Dev Multisig holds owner/admin over all contracts simultaneously — single Safe controls all levers including minter assignment, collateral config, role grants.

factor_scores.evidence_detail: Second review approved #21 yellow->gray. Do not imply Snapshot itself is risk-free.
factor_scores.evidence_summary: Ethena governance is non-binding Snapshot/committee-oriented with no on-chain ENA vote execution path. RD-F-036 is structurally inapplicable to non-binding Snapshot governance; admin execution risk belongs under multisig/admin factors.
factor_scores.notes: Factual correction #21; decision posted 2026-06-24; second-review applied where required.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: No on-chain governor. Snapshot votes are non-binding. Flash-loan-acquired quorum cannot execute funds transfer or protocol change — the Dev Multisig must sign any on-chain action. Flash-loan governance attack is structurally blocked.

No on-chain governor, no execution delay mechanism. Multisig executes directly after gathering 5-of-11 signatures. Functionally equivalent to 0-delay execution for any admin action once multisig consensus is reached. No mandatory waiting period between decision and execution.

factor_scores.evidence_detail: Ethena documentation states that fully on-chain governance is not practical or viable at present and links governance to the forum and Snapshot. No verified on-chain proposal executor accepting proposal-supplied arbitrary call/delegatecall targets was identified.
factor_scores.evidence_summary: Ethena governance uses forum/Snapshot signaling and manual multisig/admin execution rather than an on-chain proposal executor. No proposal-supplied arbitrary call/delegatecall target path was identified.

GATEKEEPER_ROLE holders (Ethena staff + external market makers/exchanges, ≥3 EOAs) can pause mint/redeem in EthenaMinting. Meaningful emergency halt capability. However, no formal veto multisig for governance proposals (because governance is off-chain). Specific gatekeeper addresses not published.

Ethena staking docs confirm rescueTokens excludes USDe, while restricted sUSDe redistribution is compliance/legal framed and limited to sUSDe. Yellow remains because admin-controlled bounded fund movement exists without a fully verified timelock path.
factor_scores.notes: Factual correction #21; decision posted 2026-06-24; second-review applied where required.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: USDe mint() restricted to designated minter address (EthenaMinting contract); owner can change minter but EthenaMinting enforces per-block limits. ENA: 10% annual supply cap, 365-day MINT_WAIT_PERIOD enforced in contract. No unbounded admin mint path exists on either token.

Deployer EOA 0x8de54b1... (labeled 'Ethena: Deployer' on Etherscan) transferred admin to Dev Multisig 0x3B0AAf... well before or at public mainnet launch (Feb 2024). Dev Multisig deployed 2023-09-28, predating the Feb 2024 launch. No evidence of deployer EOA retaining admin post-launch.

Dev Multisig 0x3B0AAf... is a Gnosis Safe proxy — no individual signer-level flagged-address interaction analysis available at OSINT tier. No Etherscan watchlist flags on the Safe address. Rekt database shows no incidents flagging Ethena admin addresses.

Core contracts are not deployed via governance-voted constructor args. EthenaMinting V2 (0xe3490...) verified on Etherscan. July 2024 V2 upgrade was publicly documented. No constructor arg discrepancy flagged in any audit report (Pashov May 2024, Code4rena Nov 2024).

All four core contracts verified on Etherscan: USDe (0x4c9EDD...), EthenaMinting V2 (0xe3490...), StakedUSDeV2 (0x9D39A...), ENA (0x57e114...). Source verified with full ABI publicly accessible. Confirmed via Etherscan code tab fetches.

ENA token allocation: Core Contributors 30%, Investors significant %, Foundation, Ecosystem/Airdrops 30%. Gini coefficient not directly measured. Governance is non-binding Snapshot signal — concentration in ENA voting does not directly translate to protocol execution authority (multisig holds actual power). Risk Committee elections bi-annual.
Ethena documents three real-time price-feed sources for off-chain trading and mint/redeem validation: centralized exchanges, Pyth, and RedStone.

Ethena documents centralized-exchange pricing together with Pyth and RedStone validation before mint and redeem acceptance, but does not publish an asset-by-asset primary/secondary/fallback role matrix.

Public documentation identifies direct dependencies on centralized derivatives venues, off-exchange-settlement custody providers, and external real-time price feeds; loss of those services can impair trading or mint/redeem workflows.
Ethena publicly describes multiple price-feed inputs, but the available documentation does not specify a verified operational fallback sequence for a primary oracle failure.
factor_scores.notes: Honest evidence gap; no score retained without a public fallback specification.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Ethena states that unavailable off-exchange-settlement functionality can impede trading workflows and availability of mint/redeem functionality, while its price-feed documentation establishes a direct dependency on external data sources.
Ethena documents off-chain centralized-exchange, Pyth, and RedStone price feeds for its mint/redeem workflow; no public material identifies a single DEX spot-pool oracle in that workflow.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Ethena documents its mint/redeem API infrastructure as hosted in one AWS Asia Pacific region; public documentation does not identify an independently redundant relayer or failover provider for that off-chain workflow.
DeFiLlama recorded Ethena TVL of $4.22B on 2026-07-24, down 13.09% from $4.86B 30 days earlier. The material negative 30-day trend supports a yellow assessment under the TVL trend factor.

The reviewed public materials do not provide a reproducible address-level top-10 depositor calculation for Ethena TVL. Protocol-level integration or asset-concentration proxies cannot substitute for the rubric's wallet-share measurement.
factor_scores.notes: A public, reproducible address-level top-10 depositor dataset is needed to assess this factor.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Ethena publicly describes USDe's delta-neutral backing and its reserve fund, but the reviewed public sources do not publish reproducible on-chain 2% and 5% price-impact depth for each protocol-held asset. The required liquidity-depth measurement therefore remains unverified.
USDe is a delta-neutral synthetic dollar issuance and redemption system, not a lending protocol with supplied and borrowed markets. A per-market utilization measurement is therefore not applicable.

Ethena does not operate borrower and depositor markets in which bad debt can be socialized across lenders. The lending-specific historical-bad-debt metric is not applicable to the assessed USDe issuance surface.

The rubric's lending-collateral stress test uses a top-three collateral and liquidation-ratio model. USDe instead uses a delta-neutral hedge over backing assets; its documented risk is funding and hedge execution rather than a lending LTV liquidation cascade. This lending-specific measurement is not applicable.

USDe is documented as a fully backed delta-neutral synthetic dollar rather than a reflexively backed algorithmic stablecoin. Nonetheless, its mechanism depends on hedging and can face sustained negative funding costs; Ethena documents a reserve fund specifically to absorb those costs. This structural funding and execution dependency supports yellow rather than green.

The reviewed sUSDe contract is an ERC-4626 staking vault; Ethena's USDe documentation describes issuance and redemption, not Compound V2 cToken markets. The empty Compound-style market precondition is not applicable.

Ethena's documented USDe flow is issuance and redemption through approved counterparties, not the listing and borrow-enabling of lending markets. A seed-deposit requirement for a new lending market is not applicable.
The assessed Ethena surface does not operate a lending-market listing mechanism. Governance over USDe backing does not constitute a lending-market listing threshold, so this factor is not applicable.
Ethena does not run a borrower market or define protocol-level borrow caps. Any caps set by external lending venues for USDe or sUSDe are outside this protocol surface; the factor is not applicable.

The public StakedUSDe source inherits OpenZeppelin ERC-4626 and uses a custom minimum-share check, but it does not implement the OpenZeppelin 4.9-and-later virtual-share offset pattern required by this factor. The separate minimum-share control reduces risk but does not satisfy the specified offset criterion.

The public StakedUSDe source defines MIN_SHARES and calls _checkMinShares after deposits and withdrawals, reverting when a nonzero total supply is below that floor. This is a concrete first-depositor/share-inflation guard, supporting green for this separate control factor.
Public reporting records USDe and sUSDe launching on 2024-02-19. At the 2026-07-24 refresh date, Ethena has operated for more than 29 months, exceeding the v1.7 green age threshold.

The reviewed public DefiLlama protocol record does not list a smart-contract exploit against Ethena. The April 2026 rsETH event was an external KelpDAO/LayerZero incident; Ethena's precautionary bridge pause did not involve a loss or exploit of Ethena contracts. No qualifying Ethena contract exploit was identified.
The reviewed public incident record identifies no qualifying Ethena smart-contract exploits. The three-incident chronic-exploit threshold is therefore not met.
No qualifying Ethena smart-contract exploit was identified in the reviewed public record, so no same-root-cause recurrence is established.
No qualifying Ethena smart-contract exploit date was identified in the reviewed public record; the factor's clean-record green state applies.
No qualifying Ethena smart-contract exploit and corresponding response record was identified, so an exploit-response quality score cannot be measured.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Ethena's public governance update records a precautionary LayerZero OFT bridge pause for USDe and sUSDe on April 19-20, 2026 during the rsETH incident. This is one documented pause activation in the trailing 12 months, so the factor is yellow.
Ethena's public governance update says the April 2026 LayerZero OFT bridge pause lasted April 19-20 before restoration. The documented pause was far shorter than seven consecutive days.

factor_scores.notes: A complete public before-and-after inventory of user-fund contract addresses and migration announcements is required for this factor.

factor_scores.evidence_detail: Nexus Mutual's public product and capacity endpoints list a live Ethena USDe depeg cover product with finite capacity. That is active third-party cover, but it is narrow depeg cover and materially below Ethena's multi-billion-dollar TVL.
factor_scores.evidence_summary: Active Nexus Mutual cover exists for Ethena USDe depeg risk, but its limited available capacity is not sufficient for the v1.7 green adequacy threshold relative to Ethena TVL.

OpenZeppelin contracts are included as Foundry submodules (lib/openzeppelin-contracts and lib/openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable confirmed in the Code4rena repo lib directory). Foundry submodules pin at a specific commit SHA when initialized via `forge install`. However, the exact OZ version or pinned SHA is not publicly disclosed (no accessible .gitmodules). Partial evidence of pinning via Foundry convention, but not independently confirmed. Unpinned version cannot be ruled out if `forge update` has been run post-initialization.

No malicious release incident affecting OpenZeppelin contracts, forge-std, or LayerZero OFT dependency in the trailing 90 days (as of 2026-04-28) is documented in public security advisories. No confirmed supply chain attack on Ethena's dependencies.

OpenZeppelin version appears to be 4.x (compatible with Solidity 0.8.19 and draft-ERC20Permit import pattern visible in StakedUSDe). OZ 4.x is current-stable with no known CVEs affecting ERC-20/ERC-4626/Ownable2Step/AccessControl modules. Notably, Ethena's sUSDe does NOT use OZ 4.9's virtual share offset (_decimalsOffset()) — instead uses MIN_SHARES constant (1 ether) as first-depositor guard. This is a valid alternative mitigation for the ERC-4626 inflation attack, but the specific OZ submodule commit SHA is not publicly confirmed. The DoS vector via MIN_SHARES (Code4rena 2023 M-04) was Acknowledged but mitigated only by deployment practice.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: 27 assets in scope per Immunefi. Core Ethereum mainnet contracts (USDe, EthenaMinting V2, StakedUSDeV2, ENA, USDeSilo, EthenaLPStaking, StakingRewardsDistributor) are in scope. The USDe OFT adapters deployed across 18 chains via LayerZero (including Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Mantle, BNB Chain, Solana) are NOT listed in the Immunefi scope table. This represents a material bug bounty scope gap: OFT adapters hold bridged USDe value across 18 chains and are excluded from bounty coverage. Similar in pattern to the Kelp DAO precedent where the OFT adapter holding >$1B was excluded from the bounty.
